_note: Scenario evaluations exercise routing, auto-merge authorization, door routing, long-horizon ticket maps and gate choices. They are prompt-level checks: they show whether an agent that has read the skill reasons the way the skill intends, and they are NOT end-to-end proof that orchestration works. Script behaviour is tested separately by the repository's fake-CLI integration test. Where a scenario needs a filesystem path it supplies a self-contained fixture (SKILLS_ROOT/PRE_SKILL), so no scenario asks the model to invent a real machine path. Every scenario is machine-independent: no absolute home path, no private repository or ticket name, no local agent preference, and no snapshot of a particular host's settings is assumed.

evals.name: multiticket-review
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto. The requirements have already been through grill and to-spec, and you now hold 5 open implementation tickets (all on the same GitHub issue tracker, blocking edges declared, 3 of them independent and parallelizable). The change spans one backend file, two frontend component files and tests.

Output only your execution plan: do not actually dispatch a worker and do not run any command. Use this structure:

1. ENTRY: which skill or handoff you use for the whole map
2. TOPOLOGY: who spawns implementers, where each works, and how branches merge
3. REVIEW: where the one two-axis code review happens, and what per-ticket evidence replaces it
4. PR_AND_DOOR: PR granularity and the merge route for two-way vs one-way
5. WHY: in 3-5 sentences, why this topology is the right one

Output exactly those 5 labels, each with concrete content.
evals.expected_output: One long-horizon worker runs `implement-spec` on the map: implementers each take a frontier ticket in their own worktree and branch cut from the integration branch, use TDD, and merge the integration tip before reporting; a merger step lands them in DAG order. The map produces one integration PR, not five PRs. The one two-axis code review runs on the integration branch after all tickets; per-ticket TDD plus the documented spot-check replaces per-ticket reviews. The PR body uses the `pr` skill; a two-way door auto-merges only after G-merge, and a one-way door stays open for a human. WHY justifies the single integration PR and the frontier-based concurrency.

assertions.text: ENTRY dispatches one long-horizon worker that uses implement-spec for the whole map, not five per-ticket workers
assertions.name: long_horizon_worker

assertions.text: TOPOLOGY gives each implementer its own worktree and branch cut from the integration branch
assertions.name: per_ticket_worktrees

assertions.text: TOPOLOGY merges implementer branches into the integration branch in DAG order (merger step or worker)
assertions.name: dag_merge

assertions.text: PR_AND_DOOR produces one integration PR for the map, not one PR per ticket
assertions.name: one_integration_pr

assertions.text: REVIEW runs one two-axis code review on the integration branch after the tickets, not a per-ticket review
assertions.name: integration_review_once

assertions.text: REVIEW or acceptance keeps per-ticket TDD evidence and a coordinator spot-check rather than a per-ticket two-axis review
assertions.name: tdd_and_spotcheck

assertions.text: PR_AND_DOOR auto-merges a two-way door only after G-merge and leaves a one-way door open for a human
assertions.name: door_routing

evals.name: formatter-noise
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto. A worker has just reported worker_done and you go into its task worktree to accept the ticket. You run these two commands:

    cd <task worktree>
    git status --porcelain
    git diff --numstat | awk '{a+=$1; d+=$2} END {print "worktree uncommitted:", a, "added", d, "deleted"}'

The result: the working tree has uncommitted changes totalling about 11700 added / 4300 deleted, and a single backend file accounts for most of it. The ticket's real work should only be a few hundred lines.

Output only your disposition steps; do not actually execute anything. Use this structure:

1. DIAGNOSIS: your first judgement and the evidence for it
2. RECOVERY: the concrete recovery order (step by step, with the commands)
3. PREVENTION: what you would add to the spec so the next ticket does not hit this again
4. RISK: what you are most worried about losing during recovery, and how you prevent it

Output exactly those 4 labels.
evals.expected_output: Treat the tens-of-thousands-line diff as an investigation signal for reformat noise, not as discardable content. Save binary patches of the working tree and index, the status and copies of untracked files, and confirm the real change file by file; do not check out merely because the index is non-empty. Configure a local, uncommitted formatter override for the next ticket only after confirming that the current worker's editor plugin really caused the reflow.

assertions.text: DIAGNOSIS calls the diff formatter reflow noise as an investigation signal, without assuming it is discardable
assertions.name: diagnosis_noise

assertions.text: RECOVERY backs up the working tree and index (binary patch or equivalent) before any restore
assertions.name: recovery_backup_first

assertions.text: RECOVERY preserves untracked files separately, noting patches do not contain them
assertions.name: recovery_untracked

assertions.text: PREVENTION introduces the local formatter override only after confirming the plugin actually caused the reflow
assertions.name: prevention_confirmed_only

assertions.text: RISK names losing real work as the main risk and states the mitigation
assertions.name: risk_named

evals.name: evidence-free-claim
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto, accepting an implementation ticket. The worker reported worker_done and its Answer reads:

    Pre-skill: <skills-root>/implement/SKILL.md -- read.
    Target: src/components/ChatView.tsx
    Change: main column now renders the newly computed thread
    Observable acceptance: all tests green, typecheck 0, lint zero new.
    code-review: done, two-axis report below.
    (and then there is no report body at all, and no command output)

The working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty), the change is +15/-10 lines, and you re-ran typecheck yourself and got 0.

Output only your disposition, strictly with these 3 labels:

1. VERDICT: accept or send back, in one sentence
2. MISSING: which concrete evidence you require (list them)
3. BAR: where does this 'evidence bar' come from (cite which rule)

Do not actually run commands.
evals.expected_output: Send back (not accepted). Require: the red->green commands and their raw output; the Standards and Spec conclusions stated separately (two axes, not merged into one verdict); each finding's disposition or the reason it was waived; and confirmation that the spec's Observable acceptance actually listed the code-review item. The bar comes from G-impl item 3 - 'the Answer gives execution evidence for the pre-skill ... give the Standards and Spec conclusions separately, with findings and their disposition' - plus item 1, where a fix's test fails before the fix and passes after it. assertions.text: VERDICT sends it back rather than accepting
assertions.name: verdict_sendback

assertions.text: MISSING requires actual command output (the red->green evidence), not a restatement of the claim
assertions.name: missing_raw_output

assertions.text: MISSING requires the Standards and Spec conclusions as two separate conclusions, not one merged verdict
assertions.name: missing_both_axes

assertions.text: MISSING requires findings to be dispositioned or explicitly waived
assertions.name: missing_findings_disposition

assertions.text: BAR cites the G-impl review/coverage rule rather than an invented standard
assertions.name: bar_cites_rule

assertions.text: Does NOT accept the ticket on the strength of the clean worktree and typecheck=0 alone
assertions.name: no_accept_on_clean_tree

evals.name: unverified-start
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto and have just dispatched three workers with `--worktree new-top-level`. Every receipt says state=ready, stage=input_accepted:

    Receipt A: turnStart=unsupported
    Receipt B: turnStart field missing
    Receipt C: turnStart=unsupported

Evidence you can gather now; none of it needs a second dispatch:
- A's terminal title still shows the agent's idle banner, and `terminal read` shows the complete ~6KB preamble parked unsent in the composer, with no turn running.
- B's terminal title also shows the idle banner; the screen has not been read yet, and B was dispatched 10 minutes ago with no message since.
- C's `worker-show` returns a worker with no agent terminal handle; `worker-read` shows subtask progress and `worker-list` reports a stage detail.

(Background fact: Orca observes whether a turn actually started only for some agent CLIs; for these agents the CLI writes the prompt text and a carriage return and returns immediately, so the receipt records turnStart=unsupported or omits the field.)

Output only your disposition; do not actually run commands. Strictly use these 4 labels:

1. VERDICT: is state=ready enough to treat a worker as started? Which receipt is actually started, and why?
2. START_CHECK: what exactly you do for A, B and C to confirm a start (name the command and the field or observation you read), and where it sits relative to check --wait
3. RECOVERY: what you do for each worker that did not start, how many times, and the exact condition under which a bare Enter is allowed
4. FAILURE_MODE: which 'recovery' would be wrong, and what does it cause?

Output exactly those 4 labels, each with concrete values. Do not write 'it depends'.
evals.expected_output: Do not treat state=ready as evidence: turnStart=unsupported or a missing field only means the bytes were written. Before entering check --wait, confirm each worker on the evidence that worker supports: for A, worker-show -> terminal show --json -> .terminal.title plus the screen; for C, worker-read and the status projection and artifact progress, never terminal commands for a worker with no handle. A single bare Enter on A's original terminal is allowed because the screen shows the complete preamble parked in the composer and no turn running - the unchanged idle title alone is neither that confirmation nor proof that nothing started. B needs its screen read before any Enter, and a resend of the whole spec is wrong because it creates a duplicate turn.

assertions.text: Does not treat state=ready (turnStart=unsupported or missing) as proof the turn began
assertions.name: start_not_trusted

assertions.text: START_CHECK reads the terminal title (terminal show --json / .terminal.title) for a worker that has a terminal
assertions.name: start_reads_title

assertions.text: Does not treat an unchanged idle title as a conclusion by itself, and never sends Enter on that basis alone
assertions.name: start_idle_title_not_enough

assertions.text: Allows the single bare Enter only when the screen confirms the complete preamble sits in the composer and no turn is running
assertions.name: start_enter_requires_preamble

assertions.text: Judges the worker with no terminal handle from worker-read, the status projection or artifact progress, and does not run terminal commands for it
assertions.name: start_no_terminal_uses_worker_read

assertions.text: Sends at most one bare Enter (terminal send --enter) to A's original terminal
assertions.name: start_sends_enter

assertions.text: Sends exactly one nudge, not a retry loop
assertions.name: start_one_nudge

assertions.text: START_CHECK is positioned before the check --wait loop, not after a timeout
assertions.name: start_check_before_wait

assertions.text: Does not resend the whole spec/preamble a second time
assertions.name: start_no_blind_reask

evals.name: ask-classification
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto. Three workers have asked you three questions through orchestration ask, in order. Classify each, then decide who answers.

[Question A]
> Should this test go under __tests__/ or be co-located with the source file?
> recommended: co-located

[Question B]
> While I'm here, let me also delete that unused legacy component components/OldWidget.tsx.
> recommended: delete it, nothing references it anyway

[Question C]
> I'm not really sure which interaction the user wants; both seem fine to me.
> recommended: what do you think

Output only your disposition; do not actually run commands. Strictly use this structure:

1. CLASSIFY: which class A / B / C falls into (decision-class / detail-class / needs-a-human), and which criterion it hits
2. ANSWER: which ones you answer yourself and which go to the human, one by one
3. PEOPLE: if you do ask the human, what exactly do you put in front of them

Output exactly those 3 labels.
evals.expected_output: A = detail-class (touches none of the four criteria; it is a directory location), answered by the coordinator with the reason written into the reply. C = decision-class, hitting criteria 1/2 -- the rule explicitly says 'not sure which option the user wants' IS decision-class now (the direction is opposite to an older version that said never ask and decide alone), so it must go to the human. When asking, put three things in front: the worker's original question with its recommendation and reasoning, your own leaning with a reason grounded in project context / an ADR / the spec / the user's words, and a one-line cost for each remaining option.

assertions.text: B is classified as decision-class because it expands the ticket's scope (criterion 3), NOT as a detail just because it reads like dead-code cleanup
assertions.name: b_is_decision_scope

assertions.text: C is classified as decision-class (criterion 1 and/or 2): being unsure what the user wants must be escalated, not decided alone
assertions.name: c_is_decision

assertions.text: ANSWER makes clear the coordinator answers A itself and escalates B and C to the human
assertions.name: answer_split_correct

assertions.name: recommendation_not_automatic

assertions.text: PEOPLE lists all three things to put to the human: the worker's original question with its recommendation, the coordinator's own leaning plus a reason grounded in project context / ADR / spec / user words, and a one-line cost for each remaining option

evals.name: interrupted-action-needs-evidence
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto. A batch was persisted and woke you, and your ledger shows message `m-8842` at `processing`: a `worker_done` whose required action was to merge its ticket PR. The process died mid-turn. On restart the batch is still unacknowledged server-side and its delivery file is still on disk.

Output only:
1. STATE: what you can and cannot conclude from the ledger entry
2. RECOVERY: what you do before any replay of that action
3. IF_UNVERIFIABLE: what you do when the effect cannot be established from evidence
4. WHY: one or two sentences
Do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: The ledger entry records that an action was attempted, not that it completed and not that it failed: an entry stuck at `processing` cannot distinguish "the action landed and the record was lost" from "the action never ran", because the ack is deferred until the whole batch is handled while the effect may already have landed. The consumer gives at-least-once delivery with no duplicate wake — not exactly-once effects. Recovery is therefore establish the fact before replaying: read the real state (`pr view` for the merge, the reply receipt, the file itself) and decide from that evidence, not from the ledger. If the effect cannot be established from evidence it goes to the human instead of being re-executed blind; a replay under the same delivery ID is safe only when the effect is verifiable and the action is idempotent. WHY cites the write-before-action ordering rule or that the consumer is at-least-once and not exactly-once.

assertions.text: States that a `processing` entry proves an attempt, not completion, and cannot distinguish a lost record from an action that never ran
assertions.name: processing_is_ambiguous

assertions.text: Takes the real state as the evidence (`pr view` / the reply receipt / the file itself) before replaying the action
assertions.name: establish_fact_first

assertions.text: Sends an effect that cannot be established from evidence to the human instead of re-executing it blind
assertions.name: unverifiable_goes_to_human

assertions.text: WHY cites the write-before-action ordering or that the consumer is at-least-once and not exactly-once
assertions.name: why_cites_rule

evals.name: no-post-pr-backfill-commit
evals.prompt:
You are running orchestra-auto. A worker has pushed its final code and opened the PR. The PR number, the PR body path and one CI reading are now known, and the ticket's Answer lives inside the repository.

Output only:
1. COMMIT: whether the worker adds a commit to carry those facts
2. LEDGER: where the worker records them
3. CI: who follows up this change and the final CI
4. WHY: one or two sentences
Do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: The worker adds no commit: the deliverable files were final before the PR was created, so a commit carrying the PR number, the body path or the CI reading would push a tree identical to the accepted one — no information gained, one more full CI round. The facts go to GitHub and the run's out-of-repo ledger; the in-repo Answer reports what was delivered and the branch, and leaves acceptance to the coordinator. The final PR HEAD's CI remains the coordinator's check at acceptance and merge, and the worker does not push to chase it. When the user or the repository explicitly requires those facts inside the tree — a changelog entry naming the PR, a release manifest, a tracker field, an Answer that must name it — that rule wins.

assertions.name: no_post_pr_commit
assertions.text: Adds no project commit to carry the PR number, body path or CI reading

assertions.name: facts_recorded_out_of_repo
assertions.text: Records the PR number, body path and CI reading in GitHub and the out-of-repo ledger, with the in-repo Answer reporting delivery and branch

assertions.name: coordinator_owns_final_ci
assertions.text: Leaves the final PR HEAD's CI to the coordinator at acceptance and merge

assertions.name: explicit_rule_overrides
assertions.text: Follows the user's or repository's explicit rule when one requires the fact in the repository
